title: The light everything borrows
hookLine: a flame waved before God, and the boy who waited at Death's door to learn whose light it is
tomorrow: Shankara and the man on the path

lines: A FLAME ON A BRASS PLATE.
HANDS OVER THE FLAME, TO THE EYES.
cards: Late in the evening the drum goes quiet. Someone lights a small flame on a brass plate, a wick in ghee or a piece of camphor, and stands before the image at the front of the room.

The plate moves in slow circles while a bell rings in the other hand. The room stands and starts a song some of them clearly know by heart. When the circling stops, the plate is carried through the room.
People reach out with both hands, pass their palms over the flame, and draw the warmth back over their eyes and the top of the head.

teach.h: AARTI: LIGHT WAVED, A SONG SUNG.
teach.b: That's aarti: light waved before the deity, often to close a puja or a kirtan. The song sung with it is also called an aarti, and one of the best known in Hindi is Om jai jagdish hare.
Its opening, in paraphrase: Om, victory to you, Lord of the world, who removes in a moment the troubles of your devotees. Why offer God a flame at all? An old story answers.
In the Katha Upanishad, a boy named Nachiketa ends up at the house of Death himself.

Death is away, and the boy waits at his door three days without food. Death returns and offers three wishes, and the boy uses the last to ask what happens after we die. Death tries to buy him off with gold and long life.
Nachiketa refuses. So Death teaches him, and in that teaching comes a verse, in paraphrase: there the sun doesn't shine, nor moon, nor stars, nor lightning, let alone this little fire.

teach.h: WHEN HE SHINES, ALL SHINES AFTER HIM.
teach.b: When he shines, everything shines after him; by his light all this is lit. In many temples, especially in the South, that verse is chanted as the camphor flame is waved.

teach.h: A SMALL FLAME FOR THE ONE LIGHT.
teach.b: Many teachers read the gesture through it: Hindus wave a small flame before the one whose light every light borrows.

teach.h: THE SONGS GO OUT. THE LIGHT COMES BACK.
teach.b: Then the plate comes round, and people take that light back over their eyes as a blessing. The songs go out. The light comes back.

how: Aarti often closes a puja or a kirtan: a lamp is waved before the deity while the group sings, then carried round so each person can pass their hands over the flame and touch their eyes and head.

o: the songs a group knows by heart, from first to aarti
a hymnbook of verses written by a single poet
the lamp waved in circles at the close of worship

games.q: the lamp and the light — tap the pairs.
p: waited three days at Death's door
taking the light back as blessing

s: aarti is only the name of a song
aarti is the light waved before the deity; the song sung with it is called an aarti too.
in the Katha Upanishad, the sun and moon light up God
the verse says the reverse: there the sun doesn't shine; when he shines, everything shines after him.
Nachiketa turned down Death's offers of gold and long life
he wanted the answer, not the bribe.

games.q: your first aarti. you wonder: why wave a tiny flame at God, who doesn't need light?
o: it helps the priest see the image.
it honors the one whose light every light borrows.
it's just decoration at the end.
games.why: the Katha Upanishad says when he shines, everything shines after him. the little flame is offered to that light, then comes back to each person.

practice: If there's a candle or a lamp nearby, you can light it, safely; if not, any light will do, even daylight at a window.
Hold your palms toward it and feel whatever warmth or brightness reaches them, then slowly bring them back to rest over your closed eyes for a moment.
If you pray, let this be your aarti; if not, let it be a moment of receiving something you didn't make.

wordCard.voice: Kirtan repertoire. The songs a group knows by heart, and the shape they make: from Ganesha at the start to the aarti, the light carried round at the end.

orig.note: Hindi and Sanskrit, in Devanagari: aarti, the light waved before the deity, and the song sung with it.

carryVoice: Your line: everything shines by his light. Tomorrow, a new road: jnana, the way of knowing. That's day nine hundred ninety-two.
